source.work: Quintilian, Institutio oratoria, Book VII, chapter 5 sections 5–13 and chapter 7 sections 1–2
source.license: The LacusCurtius page states that a one-asterisk URL is public domain and that the 1920 Loeb text/translation was proofread. This packet retains that page-level provenance.
source.owned_span: VII.5.5–13: arrangement and order of a complex case; VII.7.1–2: contrary laws and letter/intention conflict.

complete_paraphrase.content: A case must be analysed into topics and questions and those subdivisions arranged appropriately. In the example involving a hero's reward, property and marriage claims, the first question is whether the letter or intention of the law governs; subsidiary questions follow in natural order rather than as they happen to occur.

The teacher must demonstrate the natural order across many cases; arrangement depends on the specific case. The source uses analogies of painter, vase-maker and physician to distinguish general principles from case-specific skill.

Whole-case arrangement decides whether to use an exordium, continuous or subdivided facts, opponent or own arguments, strong or weak proofs, law or equity first, and which evidence/documents are read at each stage.
Parts must have internal order and cohesion; words should fit their positions and connect to what precedes and follows, producing continuity rather than a congeries.
Contrary laws raise letter and intention bases. Conflicting laws can be compared by time, quality, or the specific dispute; the source gives the hero/deserter and tyrannicide/woman examples.

typed_distinctions.reused_operation: ARRANGE(case,question_sequence) -> scoped argument order is reused across the reward/property/marriage example and the broader list of evidence/order choices.
typed_distinctions.critical_identity: The same CASE remains active while parent law-interpretation and subsidiary question slots change; order is an argument to the conclusion, not mere presentation.

worked_consequence.source_case_a: LETTER_OR_INTENTION(law) must be resolved before the hero's reward/property/marriage subquestions; changing that parent result changes the admissible child arguments.
worked_consequence.source_case_b: In contrary-law examples, the same case identity is instead routed through time, quality, or which law suffers less by contravention; the conclusion changes even when the claimant names remain.
worked_consequence.serious_rival: Treat all questions as an unordered catalogue and treat arrangement as rhetoric only. This rival retains the same topics but predicts order-insensitive child conclusions, contrary to Quintilian's explicit dependency.
worked_consequence.smallest_later_test: A complete later passage would need two occurrences of a shared question/result operator with distinct parent scope, plus a downstream consequence that changes when the parent question is reordered or resolved differently.

limits: Quintilian prescribes rhetorical arrangement; the packet does not claim an event history.
The source says exact arrangement depends on the particular case, so no universal order beyond the worked example is assumed.
No target clause, marker, or word meaning is bound.
